result: In 56 children with long COVID vs 27 matched controls on 24-h Holter, rMSSD was lower (47.4 vs 60.4, p=0.02) but VLF, LF and HF power were all markedly higher, interpreted as parasympathetic predominance; echocardiography was normal.
reason: Same Holter HRV measures but HF power was higher and authors conclude relative parasympathetic predominance, opposite to the finding's reduced vagal tone; paediatric long COVID, small sample

result: In 95 Dutch post-COVID patients aged 40-65, fatigue (FSS>=4) fell from 75.9% at 3-6 months to 57.1% 9-12 months later, 52.7% met Fukuda ME/CFS criteria by DSQ-2 (fewer met stricter definitions), and patients mapped onto 11 ME/CFS symptom clusters.
reason: Measures share of post-COVID patients meeting ME/CFS criteria, matching the selected-cohort ~51% estimate in the finding; small clinic cohort without uninfected controls

result: Meta-analysis of high-quality post-COVID studies (>4 weeks after infection) found moderate deficits vs controls in executive function (SMD -0.45), learning/memory (-0.55), complex attention (-0.54), language (-0.54) and perceptual-motor function (-0.70), with no domain-specific pattern.
reason: Same kind of domain-level cognitive meta-analysis but in post-COVID populations, so a long COVID extension rather than a replication; also finds language impaired, unlike ME/CFS

result: On 7T fMRI during a Stroop task, 31 ME/CFS patients vs 15 controls had reduced pontine nucleus to cerebellar vermis IX connectivity (p=0.027) and wider ponto-cerebellar FC impairment, with FC correlating with illness duration, memory scores and respiratory rate.
reason: Brainstem connectivity difference from the Griffith 7T group; an earlier paper than the cited Inderyas 2026, not the same study, and not independent of that group
